declarations.docstring: Forms a complex matrix indexed by conjugacy classes from a conjugacy-class-indexed family of representations.
Rewrites the product of an entry of the scaled character matrix with the conjugate of another entry using character values and the associated natural-number scale.
Assigns a natural number to each element of a group for use as its conjugacy centralizer cardinality.
The conjugacy centralizer cardinality of an element of a finite group is positive.
Complex conjugation of a finite-group character value equals the character value at the inverse element.
The conjugate transpose of the scaled character matrix is a left inverse when the indexed simple representations are pairwise nonisomorphic.
The conjugate transpose of the scaled character matrix is a right inverse when the indexed simple representations are pairwise nonisomorphic.
Sums products of character values over the indexed simple representations, giving the centralizer cardinality on equal conjugacy classes and zero otherwise.
The number of elements in a conjugacy class multiplied by the associated centralizer cardinality equals the group cardinality.
The conjugacy class of a chosen representative of a quotient class is that class.
Associates a complex scaling factor to a conjugacy class.
The square of the conjugacy-class scaling factor is the centralizer cardinality cast to the complex numbers.
The conjugacy-class scaling factor is nonzero for a finite group.
The real square root of the cast centralizer cardinality is positive.
Expresses a conjugated scaled-character entry times another entry as a quotient of character values by the two class scaling factors.
The conjugacy-class scaling factor is fixed by complex conjugation.
For a conjugation-invariant complex function, the sum over conjugacy classes weighted by reciprocal centralizer cardinalities equals the normalized sum over the group.
